# Good Output — database-modeling-skill

## Scenario

Job board SaaS. Architecture.md identified entities: `User`, `Company`, `Job`, `JobApplication`. PRD requires data retention for applications (soft delete). User email is PII.

## Produced Prisma_Schema_Proposal.prisma

```prisma
// Prisma_Schema_Proposal.prisma
// Generated by: database-modeling-skill
// Date: 2026-05-17

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider  = "postgresql"
  url       = env("DATABASE_URL")
  directUrl = env("DIRECT_URL")
}

model User {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  /// @privacy: PII
  email     String   @unique @map("email")
  /// @privacy: PII
  name      String   @map("name")
  role      UserRole @default(RECRUITER) @map("role")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  company      Company?
  applications JobApplication[]

  @@map("users")
}

enum UserRole {
  RECRUITER
  CANDIDATE
  ADMIN

  @@map("user_role")
}

model Company {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  name      String   @map("name")
  slug      String   @unique @map("slug")
  ownerId   String   @unique @map("owner_id")
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  owner User  @relation(fields: [ownerId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  jobs  Job[]

  @@map("companies")
}

model Job {
  id          String    @id @default(cuid())
  title       String    @map("title")
  description String    @map("description")
  status      JobStatus @default(DRAFT) @map("status")
  companyId   String    @map("company_id")
  createdAt   DateTime  @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt   DateTime  @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  company      Company          @relation(fields: [companyId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  applications JobApplication[]

  @@index([companyId])
  @@index([status])
  @@map("jobs")
}

enum JobStatus {
  DRAFT
  PUBLISHED
  CLOSED

  @@map("job_status")
}

model JobApplication {
  id          String            @id @default(cuid())
  jobId       String            @map("job_id")
  applicantId String            @map("applicant_id")
  status      ApplicationStatus @default(PENDING) @map("status")
  deletedAt   DateTime?         @map("deleted_at")
  createdAt   DateTime          @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  updatedAt   DateTime          @updatedAt @map("updated_at")

  job       Job  @relation(fields: [jobId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)
  applicant User @relation(fields: [applicantId], references: [id], onDelete: Restrict)

  @@index([jobId])
  @@index([applicantId])
  @@index([deletedAt])
  @@map("job_applications")
}

enum ApplicationStatus {
  PENDING
  REVIEWING
  REJECTED
  ACCEPTED

  @@map("application_status")
}
```

## Why this is a good output

- All 4 Architecture.md entities covered: `User`, `Company`, `Job`, `JobApplication`
- `@@map` on all models: `users`, `companies`, `jobs`, `job_applications`
- `@map` on all fields: `created_at`, `updated_at`, `company_id`, `owner_id`, `job_id`
- PII fields annotated: `User.email` and `User.name` carry `/// @privacy: PII`
- `cuid()` used for all primary keys — no sequential IDs
- All `@relation` annotations have explicit `onDelete`: `Cascade` or `Restrict`
- Standard timestamps on all models: `createdAt` and `updatedAt`
- Soft delete on `JobApplication`: `deletedAt DateTime?` + `@@index([deletedAt])`
- Foreign key indexes: `@@index([companyId])`, `@@index([jobId])`, `@@index([applicantId])`
- Output: `all_entities_covered: true`, `naming_convention_compliant: true`, `unclassified_pii_fields: []`
